signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Middle East Escalation
signals.text: Strait of Hormuz mine strikes and US threat of operations against Iran pushed WTI crude up +3.82% to $103.3 Friday, reinforcing NOK outperformance against an energy-vulnerable EUR. The G10 scorecard confirms a strong bilateral theme with NOK leader (+1.673%, n=2) versus EUR laggard (-1.004%, n=9), yielding an extreme 2.676% spread. Escalating Middle East shipping disruptions drive crude-linked terms of trade wider while French fiscal concerns sustain EUR underperformance into the Sydney/Tokyo open. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/EUR into the session open. Catalyst: Sydney open crude gap and the ECB meeting on 29 Oct. Risk: De-escalation statements from Tehran or Washington that pull WTI crude back below $100.
evidence: Strait of Hormuz mine strikes reported 19:32 UTC

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Leveraged Net Short + French Spread Stress
signals.text: EUR COT leveraged funds net short stands at -92,833 contracts (pctl 4, z -1.78), establishing heavily crowded short positioning as EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1204. French 10-year yields climbing above 5% and OIS carry favoring USD by +144bp keep downside momentum intact toward 1.1150 despite the stretched positioning. The ECB meeting on 29 Oct determines whether policy guidance confirms the hold bias and halts the decline. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD below the 20-day SMA at 1.1248. Catalyst: ECB meeting on 29 Oct. Risk: Short-covering rebound above 1.1250 driven by the 4th percentile crowded COT short.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Leveraged Short Squeeze + US Tariff Relief
signals.text: CAD COT leveraged funds net short stands at -89,659 contracts (pctl 15, z -1.32, 16.0% long) as USD/CAD closed Friday at 1.4013. Reports that the US will remove 50% tariffs on Canadian products combine with Canada's +1.2% August retail sales rebound to accelerate a CAD short squeeze, overcoming the +163bp USD OIS carry advantage. The BoC meeting on 28 Oct determines if the priced hike bias materializes to break spot decisively below 1.4000. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD targeting a break below 1.3980. Catalyst: BoC meeting on 28 Oct. Risk: Failure of US tariff removal to materialize alongside spot reclaiming the 20-day SMA at 1.4182.
evidence: US expected to remove 50% tariffs on Canadian goods

signals.title: USD/JPY — Downside Options Skew vs 265bp Carry Gap
signals.text: USD/JPY 25-delta risk reversals display an extreme -2.24 put skew, signaling elevated institutional demand for downside protection as spot closed Friday at 156.84. Friday's bearish wide-range bar and JPY leveraged short unwinds (-7,441 WoW to -37,820 net) pressure the pair, though the +265bp USD OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.88% vs TONA 1.23%) limits sustained downward extension. The BoJ meeting on 30 Oct resolves whether tightening forward guidance validates the put skew toward the 155.00 support zone. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY while capped under the 20-day SMA at 157.89. Catalyst: BoJ meeting on 30 Oct. Risk: BoJ delivers dovish hold guidance, prompting carry buyers to target 158.50.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Leveraged Longs vs Negative ESI Divergence
signals.text: AUD COT leveraged funds net long stands at +44,978 contracts (67.9% long) after closing Friday at 0.7039. Australia's negative ESI (-5.7) and an unemployment surprise jump to 4.7% (z=+4.04σ) run counter to the priced RBA hike bias and the +72bp AONIA carry advantage, exposing long positioning to liquidation. The RBA meeting on 3 Nov determines whether the central bank confirms the hike bias or validates the labor market slowdown. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD with downside unwinding risk toward 0.6980. Catalyst: RBA meeting on 3 Nov. Risk: RBA delivers an explicit pre-commitment to hike, invalidating positioning unwind pressures.
evidence: AUD ESI: -5.7 with unemployment rate shock z=+4.04σ
